- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.7) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce peak overshoots by 5–10% to avoid overreacting to short-term momentum.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is falling, avoid excessive downward bias — adjust downward only if 3+ consecutive days show negative sentiment.
- After a spike in price (forecast > 75), model tends to overcorrect — reduce forecast by 2–5% in next 3–5 days to allow mean reversion.
- When sentiment is mixed (±0.3–0.6) and price is volatile, apply smoothing: reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% to avoid overfitting to recent noise.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast for 3+ days, apply downward bias correction: subtract 1–3% from next forecast if sentiment remains neutral or slightly negative.
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is > 10% above recent 18-day average, reduce by 5–10% if sentiment is weak or negative — avoid overconfidence in long-term trends.
- If sentiment is consistently positive but price drops sharply (e.g., >5% in 3 days), reduce forecast slope to prevent “sentiment-driven overcorrection.”
